The Fantasy Arcade is a system-agnostic collection of 73 playable tavern games, casino tables, puzzles, performances and tactical arena contests for Foundry VTT. Every game runs on the GM’s client, uses imaginary points only and never changes your characters’ sheets, gold or items.

Opening the arcade

  • Click the Fantasy Arcade button in the lower-left corner of the screen, or run game.pactsFantasyArcade.open().
  • A GM must be connected: the GM’s client is the table’s referee.

Starting a table

  1. Pick a game in the library. Each game page shows its art, a guided lesson and these rules.
  2. Press Create a multiplayer table. Other players see it under Active tables and can Join.
  3. The GM can add AI opponents (they play themselves) or GM-controlled NPCs (the GM plays them). The GM can switch an NPC between the two at any time.
  4. Press Start match. Two-player shared games automatically add an AI rival if you start alone.

Kinds of table

  • Independent challenges — everyone plays their own copy and compares scores (most dice, tavern and festival games).
  • Shared tables — turn-by-turn games on one board (cards, board games, arenas).
  • Co-operative puzzles — the whole party moves the same mechanism; players may join mid-puzzle.

GM Pack Studio

Create world-saved content packs: Trivia (4–80 questions), Story scenes for Ispin’s Impossible Tale (4–80), Rune doors (4–80), a Three-Dragon Slots configuration, and linked Puzzle books (1–24 nodes). Select a pack in the library before creating its table.

Puzzle Forge

Generate reproducible riddle books by seed and difficulty, then bind any puzzle to a scene Region or Tile. When a token enters the trigger the puzzle opens for that player; solving it can reveal or hide a Tile or open or close a door Wall. Only declarative effects are possible — no scripts are stored in packs.

Tournament Hall

Run 2-, 4- or 8-competitor single-elimination brackets for the card and board games and the 1v1 arena contests. Each pairing launches a real table; decisive results advance automatically, and the GM may adjudicate draws (recorded in the audit log).

Character links

In a lobby the GM may link a seat to a world Actor (Imagi-Nations, D&D 5e, Pathfinder 2e or Daggerheart). Links are read-only: luck games ignore them; three physical contests (Arm-Wrestling, Kattal’s Hammer, Darts) accept a modest +0 to +2 assistance, and arena games choose a fitting kit. Nothing on the sheet is ever changed.

All fourteen arena and performance games share one tactical engine on a 9×7 grid.

  • Arena turn: you have 2 action points (AP). Choose an ability, then click a highlighted square (or use a self-targeted ability). Stamina and focus pay for abilities; at the start of your turn you regain 2 stamina and 1 focus, your guard fades by 1 and cooldowns tick down.
  • Damage = the ability’s base + half your Power (rounded down) + 0–2 + any Aim bonus. The target subtracts its Guard, Dodge bonus, +2 if standing in cover and +2 if hidden (maximum 10 total); an exposed target takes +2. Each hit strips 2 Guard.
  • Terrain: pillars block movement and line of sight · cover gives +2 defence · spotlights add +3 to performances · slime drains stamina · hazards and pit traps deal damage.
  • Line of sight is required for spells, ranged attacks and performances.
  • NPC difficulty (set by the GM in the lobby): 1 Casual, 2 Skilled, 3 Tactical lookahead.
  • The GM can pause an arena, take over an NPC mid-bout, or hand it back to the AI.

All stakes are fictional points; the arcade must never be used for real money or valuable property. Foundry module sockets are not a secure channel, so play with people you trust.

Call it in the air.

A pure guessing game with an enchanted coin: the crowned face is Heads, the dragon face is Tails.

At a glance

  • Players: Independent challenge: every seat plays its own copy, side by side, and the shared leaderboard compares final scores. Add AI rivals or GM-controlled NPCs for company.
  • Length: 3–15 flips (GM chooses: 3, 5, 9 or 15)
  • Goal: Score the most points by correctly predicting each flip.

Setup

  • Choose the variant when creating the table: Classic or Streak.
  • Choose the number of rounds: 3, 5, 9 or 15.

On your turn

  1. Call Heads or Tails.
  2. The coin flips (a true 50/50) and the result is shown.

Scoring

  • Classic: +1 point for each correct call.
  • Streak: a correct call scores your current streak (1, then 2, then 3…). A miss resets the streak to 0.

End of the game

After the chosen number of flips. Highest total wins.

Tips

  • There is no pattern to read — every flip is independent.
  • Streak mode rewards nerve: long runs snowball quickly.

Higher, lower… or dare the dragon’s eye?

A d12 “eye” is showing. Predict whether the next d12 will be higher, lower or exactly equal, and decide when to bank your streak.

At a glance

  • Players: Independent challenge: every seat plays its own copy, side by side, and the shared leaderboard compares final scores. Add AI rivals or GM-controlled NPCs for company.
  • Length: Up to 8 calls
  • Goal: Bank the largest streak before a wrong call wipes it out.

Setup

  • One d12 is rolled face up.

On your turn

  1. Call Higher, Lower or Equal — or Bank your current streak.
  2. A new d12 is rolled and becomes the face for the next call.

Scoring

  • Correct Higher/Lower: streak +1.
  • Correct Equal: streak +4 (a 1-in-12 shot).
  • Bank: your streak becomes your score and the game ends.

End of the game

A wrong call ends the game with 0 banked. After 8 correct calls your streak is banked automatically.

Tips

  • Extremes are your friend: on a 2, Higher wins 10 times in 12.
  • On a 6 or 7 the odds are nearly even — a good moment to bank.

Push your luck — but beware the twin fangs.

Roll two six-sided dice again and again to build a pile of points at risk, then bank before the serpent bites.

At a glance

  • Players: Independent challenge: every seat plays its own copy, side by side, and the shared leaderboard compares final scores. Add AI rivals or GM-controlled NPCs for company.
  • Length: 5 rounds
  • Goal: Bank the highest total across five rounds.

Setup

  • Your at-risk pile starts each round at 0.

On your turn

  1. Roll: add both dice to the at-risk pile.
  2. If the two dice match (any doubles) the serpent bites: the at-risk pile is lost and the round ends.
  3. Bank at any time to add the pile to your score and end the round.

Scoring

  • Banked points only. Nothing is scored for an unbanked pile.

End of the game

After five rounds (banked or bitten). Highest total wins.

Tips

  • Doubles come up 1 roll in 6. Most experts bank somewhere between 14 and 20.

Name the omen; let the kobold roll.

Each round you declare an omen, then a kobold seer rolls a d4, a d8 and a d12.

At a glance

  • Players: Independent challenge: every seat plays its own copy, side by side, and the shared leaderboard compares final scores. Add AI rivals or GM-controlled NPCs for company.
  • Length: 5 rounds
  • Goal: Score the most points by choosing omens that come true.

Setup

  • Nothing to prepare.

On your turn

  1. Choose one omen:
  2. • Ascending — d4 < d8 < d12 (about 37%).
  3. • Same parity — all three dice odd, or all even (25%).
  4. • Low — total of 11 or less (about 34%).
  5. • High — total of 16 or more (about 34%).
  6. The kobold rolls all three dice.

Scoring

  • Same parity pays 3 points. Every other omen pays 2 points.

End of the game

After five omens.

Tips

  • All four omens are close in expected value; Ascending is the steadiest, Same parity the swingiest.

Three dice, one reroll, beat the dealer.

Roll three dice, keep the ones you like, reroll the rest once, then compare totals with Grukk the goblin dealer.

At a glance

  • Players: Independent challenge: every seat plays its own copy, side by side, and the shared leaderboard compares final scores. Add AI rivals or GM-controlled NPCs for company.
  • Length: 5 rounds
  • Goal: Win the most showdowns against the dealer.

Setup

  • Each round starts with no dice.

On your turn

  1. Roll three dice.
  2. Click dice to hold them (held dice glow).
  3. Settle: every unheld die is rerolled once, then the dealer rolls three fresh dice.

Scoring

  • Beat the dealer’s total: +2.
  • Tie: +1.
  • Lose: 0.

End of the game

After five showdowns.

Tips

  • Holding 4s, 5s and 6s and rerolling the rest is a strong default.

Four dice, one reroll, build a pattern.

A four-dice pattern game: roll, optionally reroll unheld dice once, then bank the pattern.

At a glance

  • Players: Independent challenge: every seat plays its own copy, side by side, and the shared leaderboard compares final scores. Add AI rivals or GM-controlled NPCs for company.
  • Length: 5 rounds
  • Goal: Bank the most valuable patterns.

Setup

  • Each round starts with no dice.

On your turn

  1. First roll: four dice.
  2. Hold any dice, then optionally reroll the rest once.
  3. Bank the result.

Scoring

  • Pattern bonus + the sum of all four dice.
  • Four of a kind +40 · Three of a kind +24 · Two pair +18 · One pair +10 · No pattern +0.

End of the game

After five banked rounds.

Tips

  • A pair of sixes already banks 10 + the dice; chasing quads is worth it only from a triple.

Spin, hold, respin.

Three enchanted reels, each with six symbols. Hold the symbols you like and respin the rest once.

At a glance

  • Players: Independent challenge: every seat plays its own copy, side by side, and the shared leaderboard compares final scores. Add AI rivals or GM-controlled NPCs for company.
  • Length: 5 spins
  • Goal: Collect the largest payout.

Setup

  • The GM may assign a custom Slots pack with six symbols and its own payout table.

On your turn

  1. Spin all three reels.
  2. Click any symbol to hold it, then respin the unheld reels once — or bank immediately.
  3. Bank the result.

Scoring

  • Default payouts: three matching symbols 12 · any two matching 2 · the special sequence of the first three symbols (in any order) 5 · anything else 0.
  • Custom packs may change all three payouts.

End of the game

After five banked spins.

Tips

  • With a pair showing, hold it and respin the third reel: a 1-in-6 shot at the triple.

Seven bones, three throws, don’t show three skulls.

Throw seven skull dice up to three times, holding the good ones. The skull face (⚀) is deadly.

At a glance

  • Players: Independent challenge: every seat plays its own copy, side by side, and the shared leaderboard compares final scores. Add AI rivals or GM-controlled NPCs for company.
  • Length: 5 rounds
  • Goal: Bank the highest-value hauls without busting.

Setup

  • Each round starts with no dice.

On your turn

  1. Toss all seven dice.
  2. Hold any dice and throw the rest again — up to three throws in total.
  3. Bank whenever you like.

Scoring

  • If three or more skulls show when you bank, the round scores 0.
  • Otherwise score the total of every non-skull die, +10 bonus if no skulls show at all.

End of the game

After five banked rounds.

Tips

  • Held skulls still count against you — only reroll a skull if you can afford the risk.

Thirteen rows, five dice, three rolls.

A complete scorecard dice game. Each round you get up to three rolls of five dice, then must fill one unused scorecard row.

At a glance

  • Players: Independent challenge: every seat plays its own copy, side by side, and the shared leaderboard compares final scores. Add AI rivals or GM-controlled NPCs for company.
  • Length: 13 rounds
  • Goal: Finish all thirteen rows with the highest total.

Setup

  • An empty 13-row scorecard.

On your turn

  1. Roll five dice. Hold any dice and reroll the rest, up to three rolls per round.
  2. Choose an unused row. The button shows what the row would score.

Scoring

  • Ones–Sixes: the sum of dice showing that number.
  • Three of a kind / Four of a kind: sum of all dice if you have at least that many matching.
  • Full house (three + two): 25.
  • Small straight (four in a row): 30.
  • Large straight (five in a row): 40.
  • Five of a kind: 50.
  • Chance: sum of all dice.
  • A row that does not qualify scores 0 — sometimes you must sacrifice one.

End of the game

After the thirteenth row is filled.

Tips

  • Keep Chance for emergencies.
  • Five of a kind is worth chasing from four of a kind with rolls to spare.

Haul the chain — but not too far.

Tug a giant’s weighted chain. Each successful pull builds tension and points, but every pull is harder than the last.

At a glance

  • Players: Independent challenge: every seat plays its own copy, side by side, and the shared leaderboard compares final scores. Add AI rivals or GM-controlled NPCs for company.
  • Length: 4 hauls
  • Goal: Bank the biggest hauls.

Setup

  • Tension and haul start at 0 each round.

On your turn

  1. Haul: roll a d6. You need 2 + tension or more (2+, 3+, 4+, then 5+ at most).
  2. Success: add 2 + tension to the unbanked haul, then tension rises by 1.
  3. Failure: the chain slips — the unbanked haul is lost and the round ends.
  4. Secure the rope at any time after a successful pull to bank the haul.

Scoring

  • Banked haul only. Sample run: 2, then 3, then 4 = 9 banked after three pulls.

End of the game

After four rounds (banked or slipped).

Tips

  • Two or three pulls is the sweet spot; the fourth pull fails a third of the time.

Establish the point, then chase it before a seven.

A fantasy version of the classic two-dice point game.

At a glance

  • Players: Independent challenge: every seat plays its own copy, side by side, and the shared leaderboard compares final scores. Add AI rivals or GM-controlled NPCs for company.
  • Length: 5 hands
  • Goal: Win the most hands.

Setup

  • Each hand begins on the come-out roll.

On your turn

  1. Come-out roll: 7 or 11 wins the hand immediately; 2, 3 or 12 loses it immediately.
  2. Any other total (4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10) becomes your point.
  3. Keep rolling: rolling the point again wins; rolling a 7 first loses. Other totals do nothing.

Scoring

  • Each won hand: +3.

End of the game

After five decided hands.

Tips

  • 6 and 8 are the easiest points to make; 4 and 10 the hardest.

Name a rune, roll three bones.

Pick a rune value from 1 to 6, then three dice are cast.

At a glance

  • Players: Independent challenge: every seat plays its own copy, side by side, and the shared leaderboard compares final scores. Add AI rivals or GM-controlled NPCs for company.
  • Length: 6 rounds
  • Goal: Collect the most matching runes.

Setup

  • Nothing to prepare.

On your turn

  1. Choose a rune value 1–6.
  2. Three dice are rolled.

Scoring

  • +2 per die showing your rune.
  • +4 triad bonus if all three dice match each other (any value).

End of the game

After six rounds.

Tips

  • Every rune is equally likely — choose your lucky number.

Hidden cups, rising bids, someone is lying.

Each goblin hides five dice under a cup. Players bid on how many dice of a face exist across all cups, and anyone may call the bluff.

At a glance

  • Players: 2–6 players at one shared table (AI goblins fill empty seats).
  • Length: Until one goblin keeps dice, or 18 challenges
  • Goal: Be the last goblin with dice — or hold the most dice when the 18-challenge limit is reached.

Setup

  • Everyone starts with five dice, rolled in secret. You only ever see your own cup.

On your turn

  1. Bid: claim “at least N dice showing face F” across every cup. Each bid must raise the previous one — more dice, or the same quantity with a higher face.
  2. Challenge: instead of bidding, call the previous bid a lie.
  3. On a challenge every cup is revealed and the matching dice are counted.

Scoring

  • If the bid was true (enough dice), the challenger loses one die.
  • If the bid was false, the bidder loses one die.
  • A goblin with no dice is eliminated. After each challenge, press Next to re-roll every cup.

End of the game

When one goblin has dice left, or after 18 challenges (most dice wins; ties are draws).

Tips

  • Expect about one-sixth of the unseen dice to show any given face — plus what you can see in your own cup.

Twenty-one, dragon-style.

A twenty-one game played with mystical cards valued 1–12 against the dealer.

At a glance

  • Players: Independent challenge: every seat plays its own copy, side by side, and the shared leaderboard compares final scores. Add AI rivals or GM-controlled NPCs for company.
  • Length: 5 hands
  • Goal: Finish each hand closer to 21 than the dealer without going over.

Setup

  • You and the dealer each receive two cards. Only the dealer’s first card is visible.

On your turn

  1. Hit: take another card. Reaching 21 or more ends your turn automatically.
  2. Stand: stop drawing.
  3. Double (first two cards only): take exactly one more card and double the stakes for this hand.
  4. A card showing 1 counts as 11 whenever that would not take you over 21.
  5. The dealer then draws until reaching at least 17.

Scoring

  • Win: +2 (+4 doubled). Tie at 21 or under: +1 (+2 doubled). Bust or lose: 0.

End of the game

After five hands.

Tips

  • Stand on 17+; hit 11 or less; double on 10–11 when the dealer shows a low card.

Three cards, one swap, beat the goblin dealer.

A short poker game using a 20-card wyvern deck: ranks 1–5 in four suits (Sun, Moon, Leaf, Flame).

At a glance

  • Players: Independent challenge: every seat plays its own copy, side by side, and the shared leaderboard compares final scores. Add AI rivals or GM-controlled NPCs for company.
  • Length: 5 hands
  • Goal: Hold a better three-card hand than the dealer.

Setup

  • You and the dealer receive three cards each. The dealer’s cards stay hidden.

On your turn

  1. Swap one card for the top of the deck, or Keep all three.
  2. Both hands are revealed and compared.

Scoring

  • Hand ranking (best first): Straight flush · Three of a kind · Flush · Straight · Pair · High card. Ties within a rank go to the higher pair, then the higher card total.
  • Win +2 · Tie +1 · Lose 0.

End of the game

After five hands.

Tips

  • In this small deck a pair is common (about 42%) — flushes are genuinely rare.

Two private cards, five shared, fictional chips only.

A complete Texas-style hold’em with fixed, bounded wagers of fictional points.

At a glance

  • Goal: Unhorse your rival by knockout or win on points.

Setup

  • Both riders use the Beast Rider kit (32 HP, 15 stamina).

  1. Arena turn: you have 2 action points (AP). Choose an ability, then click a highlighted square (or use a self-targeted ability). Stamina and focus pay for abilities; at the start of your turn you regain 2 stamina and 1 focus, your guard fades by 1 and cooldowns tick down.
  2. Damage = the ability’s base + half your Power (rounded down) + 0–2 + any Aim bonus. The target subtracts its Guard, Dodge bonus, +2 if standing in cover and +2 if hidden (maximum 10 total); an exposed target takes +2. Each hit strips 2 Guard.

  • Each hit earns half its damage as score.

Knockout, or the judges after 18 rounds.

A co-operative stealth trial: cross the vault, reach the prize and extract before the patrol raises the alarm.

At a glance

  • Players: 2 co-operative Shadowrunners.
  • Length: 12 rounds, or the alarm
  • Goal: Extract the prize while the alert is 6 or less.

Setup

  • Patrol alert starts at 0 of 7. Cover squares are scattered across the floor.

On your turn

  1. Arena turn: you have 2 action points (AP). Choose an ability, then click a highlighted square (or use a self-targeted ability). Stamina and focus pay for abilities; at the start of your turn you regain 2 stamina and 1 focus, your guard fades by 1 and cooldowns tick down.
  2. Alert rises by 1 at the end of every round, and by 1 whenever you move onto open ground while not hidden.
  3. Fade into shadow hides you (and lowers alert by 1) until you attack. Distract patrol lowers alert by 3.
  4. Extract quietly (2 AP) within one square of the prize.

Scoring

  • Extracting scores +20.

End of the game

Success on extraction; failure if the alert reaches 7 or time runs out.

Tips

  • One runner distracts while the other moves.
